question: a5be53f269ac's clause 3 says a run casting three tickets makes exactly three reader calls; since 0f4448fdb930 one outline check is the union of 3 valid reads, so the run makes 9. Is the tooth wrong (count one check per cast, every call reported in its record, none overlapping) or is the outline check wrong?
why_it_blocks: a5be's tooth 3 encodes its falsifier clause 3 ('exactly three reader calls'); the fix stops it counting one read per cast, so the constraint narrows and needs a recorded ruling in the same act
answer: The tooth is wrong; the outline check is right. a5be's clause 3 was written when one check was one read, and its why was cost and burst: each cast costs one check, and the reads never run at once. 0f4448fdb930 (2026-11-20, measured: one read cleared a real contradiction 1 or 2 times in 5) made one check the union of UNION=3 valid reads, on purpose, so 9 calls for 3 casts is the designed cost, not a burst. The tooth now asserts what clause 3 was for: exactly one ran:true check per cast, every reader call reported in its cast's record (calls == sum of each record's meta), an equal read count per check, and no two calls overlapping. It still reds on a second check per cast, a stray read outside a record, or an overlap. The count is read from the records because the tester may not import codemother's UNION (RULE 1). Adjudicated why against why, CC's, per Akien 2026-11-01: 'look at both their why's and ajudicate from there'.
